# Keep viewport scaling and Flutter layout state coherent across native resizing

## Platform difference

Native viewport changes and embedded platform views can expose scaling, input and widget-lifetime assumptions in shared Flutter layouts.

## Implementation

Pica Comic patches specific embedding sources to stabilize viewport DPI and separately preserves controllers/scroll positions across responsive reparenting. PiliPlus temporarily sets custom app scale to 1.0 for an OH CAPTCHA platform view and restores it on disposal. NJU opts out of bottom-inset Scaffold resizing on one form and ensures the native FlutterPage fills its container.

## Applicability

These are different layers of one coordinate/lifetime contract: embedding metrics, platform-view coordinates and Dart state. Apply each fix only to its documented symptom/version.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

A source-text HAR patch can drift or affect generated dependencies unexpectedly. A page-specific keyboard fix does not prove that OH keyboards or Flutter resizing are generally broken. Do not discard controllers merely because an adaptive layout changes parents.

## Verification

Test multiple densities, window changes, keyboard opening, hit testing, scroll position retention and restoration of any temporary scale changes.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.

updates.notes: Native Index replaces global px2vp with instance UIContext.px2vp and adds densityUpdate listener, re-reads physical window rect and unregisters exact callback. Later safe-area bridge merges TYPE_SYSTEM/TYPE_CUTOUT edges on every device instead of prior phone-only cutout policy; computes leading/trailing distances, converts once in Dart and merges by max. Consumer requires valid query/error fallback, documented window-mode capability and avoids treating theoretical PC-fix subject as runtime result. Official OpenHarmony UIContext/density observer/window docs checked. Related fork density patch identical; safe-area patch differs in surrounding app code, selected native mechanism compared rather than called identical. No display-size/multidisplay/input/device test.
